title: Ledger and Bridge
premise: In the winter of 1918, Emrys Lockridge keeps the light at Gwennol Point and keeps her past buried beneath a dead husband's name. When a census taker records an answer she never meant to give, her true identity — and the ledger proving her late husband smuggled deserters to safety — becomes evidence that could hang surviving families, including her own brother. To protect them, Emrys must carry the ledger across three military checkpoints before the armistice freezes the courts' authority, deciding whether surrender or destruction will save more lives. She burns half the pages and delivers the rest as testimony, trading her invisibility for a public reckoning that finally lets her belong to herself.
about_author: Casper Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing coastal station logs from the First World War era. Ledger and Bridge is their first novel, drawn from the marginalia of keepers who recorded weather in ink and everything else in silence.

chapters.title: The Weight of Weather
chapters.summary: Emrys tends the Gwennol Point light alone through the first great storm, establishing her routines, her grief for husband Tomas, and her careful habit of answering no question fully. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: competent solitude masking loneliness.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Census taker Bronwen Hale arrives by supply boat and notices discrepancies in the station register — a wife listed nowhere, initials scratched out. Her casual question about 'the Lockridge before you' rattles Emrys into a lie she immediately regrets. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: the crack in the wall of invisibility.

chapters.title: What Tomas Left
chapters.summary: Searching for lamp oil, Emrys finds Tomas's hidden ledger recording payments, names, and routes used to move deserters and draft resisters across the channel. Among the names: her brother Idris, still alive and still reachable. POV: Emrys with a flashback to Tomas. Emotional beat: grief curdling into fear.

chapters.title: The Visitor Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: A naval officer arrives claiming to follow up on census irregularities; Emrys realizes Bronwen's paperwork has been requisitioned. She hides the ledger inside the clock mechanism and performs the role of dull widow so well it frightens her. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: performance as survival, and its cost.

chapters.title: Bronwen Returns
chapters.summary: Bronwen comes back off-duty, confessing she copied one page before the requisition — and that the officer, Captain Vey, suspects smuggling rings tied to the armistice negotiations. Reluctantly, the two women form an uneasy alliance. POV: alternating Emrys and Bronwen. Emotional beat: wary trust between women on opposite sides of curiosity.

chapters.title: Checkpoint at Porth Aman
chapters.summary: Emrys takes the coastal road toward Idris with the ledger sewn into her coat, bluffing through the first checkpoint using her keeper's authority papers. She learns Vey has offered amnesty-for-names to informants, meaning someone may already be selling. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Bridge at Nant Fawr
chapters.summary: At the second checkpoint, a young sentry recognizes Idris's name from wanted circulars; Emrys talks her way past but is now marked. Crossing the flooded bridge, she nearly loses the ledger to the river and understands she cannot outrun this — only choose what survives. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Idris
chapters.summary: Emrys finds Idris living under another man's name in a quarry village. He wants the ledger burned; she wants it delivered as proof that the smuggling saved lives worth pardoning. Their argument reopens twenty years of family wounds about who got to be safe. POV: Emrys and Idris. Emotional beat: belonging contested by blood.

chapters.title: The Third Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Armistice rumors stall the trains; Vey himself waits at the final checkpoint, having traced Bronwen's copied page. Emrys surrenders the ledger voluntarily, gambling that full disclosure beats discovery — and that Bronwen can verify the rescue count. POV: Emrys, with Bronwen arriving as witness. Emotional beat: climax — visibility chosen at last, at maximum risk.

chapters.title: Light Kept Burning
chapters.summary: The armistice is signed; a tribunal spares Idris and the named families, and Emrys returns to Gwennol Point no longer hiding behind Tomas's name. Bronwen visits with the census corrected in Emrys's own hand. The light turns, and she lets herself be seen. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: resolution — identity claimed, belonging earned.
